<!-- meta:issue:110 -->
<!-- workflow-source:local_request -->
Source: #110. Refs #110; source acceptance remains with the parent.

Creating a comparison now prints an opaque ID backed by a versioned local JSON record of ordered DOCX paths and SHA-256 hashes. `export-docx --blackline ID` reopens that record in a fresh process, verifies the exact input buffers, and calls the existing native tracked-changes renderer. The boolean file-pair invocation still works.

Malformed/path/unknown IDs, missing sources, changed bytes, replacement input paths, and source/record output aliases fail before output publication. README documents record fields, local storage, source retention, and distinct DOCX/package versus extracted-PDF fidelity. No workflow infrastructure, hosted service, database, PDF conversion, or semantic pairing change.

Validation:
- 54 focused tests passed; public CLI creation, fresh-process ID-only export, real native DOCX acceptance/rejection reconstruction, and file-pair compatibility.
- Deliberately disconnecting SHA-256 verification caused all 4 named `SHA256_CHECK_DISCONNECTION` assertions to fail. Byte-identical restoration passed all 25 comparison tests.
- Isolated full suite: 503 passed, 89.02% coverage against the unchanged 80% floor. The first shared-interpreter run had 502 passed/1 install-permission failure; its raw log/JUnit is retained. The same unmodified install test passed in a temporary venv.
- Ruff and Black passed. Changed-module mypy passed with silent imported modules. Full mypy remains FAIL: two unused-ignore errors in unchanged `docling_segmenter.py:111-112`.
- Installed Ruff/Black/mypy are 0.16.7/26.5.1/2.3.1, older than the repository pins; pinned-version results remain unknown.
- Portable replay passed. No hosted CI wait, merge, source closure, Office launch or computer-wide approval.

Evidence: [`docs/evidence/issue-110/README.md`](docs/evidence/issue-110/README.md), including real JUnit/logs, deliberate-break hashes, code hashes, synthetic DOCX inputs/output, SHA256SUMS and explicit portable replay. Advisor consult and considered declines are recorded; the live ledger lock was sandbox-denied, so a captured registry copy was consulted without claiming a shared-ledger heartbeat.

Ownership refresh found no source native reservations/completions, no recorded workflow attempts, no linked PR across any head, and no target remote branch. No source agent labels were applied. This ready PR is handed back for independent adjudication; local verification does not establish hosted acceptance.

## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
README.md:19-26 says the planned `--blackline <id>` interface from issue #15 is not implemented because no persisted comparison-ID lookup contract connects ingest (#8) and blackline (#10). Verified current state: `src/doc_lineage/cli.py:49` defines `--blackline` as `store_true` and requires `--original`/`--modified`, so an ID-only invocation exits 2. `ingest_document` (`src/doc_lineage/ingest.py:242`) publishes segments and evidence, and `src/doc_lineage/blackline.py:30` produces in-memory section pairs and NDJSON edges; nothing persists a comparison that `export_docx_redline` (`src/doc_lineage/export/docx_redline.py:6`) can resolve. A user must resupply both paths every time and cannot reproduce an export against the exact bytes originally compared. This is a missing capability, not a regression.

Current source readback: `src/doc_lineage/cli.py:49` at `b9daca70b27f452d62d8c6ccdb3bcd3b5dc7a783` (file SHA-256 `7a109fd42eef1873b7976ab3894540c136c022270237c71467626ce47473b096`). Earlier detailed line ranges and reproductions retain their reviewed-commit provenance; intervening anchor changes were checked for relevance.

#### Tasks
- [x] Add a "Comparison records" section to README.md (replacing the not-implemented paragraph at lines 19-26) defining the record fields, ID generation, store location and verification rules.
- [x] In `src/doc_lineage/blackline.py` (after `emit_lineage_edges_ndjson`, line 188), add functions to write a record (ordered `original_sha256`, `modified_sha256`, input paths, schema version) and load by ID, raising `ValueError` for unknown IDs.
- [x] In `src/doc_lineage/cli.py:49`, add a subcommand or option that creates a comparison from two DOCX paths and prints the ID; accept `--blackline <id>` on `export-docx` without breaking the boolean file-pair form.
- [x] In `_run_export_docx` (`src/doc_lineage/cli.py:99`), resolve the ID, re-read both inputs, verify SHA-256 against the record, and pass bytes to `export_docx_redline`.
- [x] Add tests to `tests/test_cli.py` covering create, new-process reopen, ID-only export, unknown ID, missing input and changed bytes.
- [x] Extend `tests/export/test_docx_redline_golden.py:84` style assertions to check the ID-driven export reconstructs original and modified text when changes are rejected and accepted.

#### Acceptance criteria
- [x] `pytest tests/test_cli.py -k comparison` passes: a comparison created from two synthetic DOCX files is reopened in a fresh invocation and exported by ID alone.
- [x] Deliberate-break gate: temporarily skip the SHA-256 check in `_run_export_docx`; the changed-bytes comparison test in `tests/test_cli.py` must FAIL. Revert afterward.
- [x] Passing a filesystem path as the `--blackline` value exits nonzero with a message that it is not a comparison ID.
- [x] `pytest tests/test_cli.py` still passes, proving the file-pair form is unchanged, and README.md no longer says the ID workflow is not implemented.
